title: What to Retrieve for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation? An Empirical Study and Beyond
summary: The original AllianceCoder pipeline performs repository-level code generation through three stages: repository API processing (LLM generates natural-language descriptions for all APIs, encoded as vectors), query processing (LLM decomposes the user query into implementation steps and retrieves candidate APIs via semantic matching), and context-integrated code generation (retrieved APIs plus current-file context fed to LLM for final generation).

This reproduction replaces that multi-stage RAG pipeline with a single Claude Sonnet 4.6 call per task using two prompt strategies: a black-box prompt (Prompt A) that requests 5 distinct implementations with no methodology guidance, and an informed prompt (Prompt B) that provides a 6-step methodology covering symbol cataloguing, spec decomposition, API matching, candidate expansion, implementation, and output formatting.
